summary: Pole tower at the Dufur Ranger Station in Wasco County, built 1933-34 and since removed; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: The tower is gone. No source dates its removal.

access.note: The site is inside a Forest Service ranger station compound. No source says whether visitors may enter the grounds.

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry (per FFLOS); firelookout.com and Rex's page place it at the Forest Service compound

events.note: Constructed September 1933 by Don Bodley's crew using CCC men (Rex's page); firelookout.com also gives 1933
FFLOS gives 1934 and credits the Oregon Forestry Department; conflicts with the 1933 sources
Panorama photographs taken June 30, 1934 by Robert Cooper

evidence.supports: built September 1933 by CCC men under Don Bodley (Rex's page dates the work to September 1933)
evidence.quote: September 1933: Don Bodley, Carpenter Foreman, has constructed a lookout tower at the Dufur Ranger Station using CCC men from a side camp of Friend Camp, F-9.

evidence.supports: 20-foot pole tower at the FS compound, dated 1933, now gone
evidence.quote: 1933: 20' pole tower at FS compound. Gone.

evidence.supports: tower stood in the town of Dufur
built 1934 by the Oregon Forestry Department at the Dufur headquarters compound; now gone
evidence.quote: This pole tower, built by the Oregon Forestry Department at the Dufur headquarters compound in 1934, is now gone.

evidence.supports: panorama photographs taken June 30, 1934 by Robert Cooper
evidence.quote: June 30, 1934: Panorama photos taken by Robert Cooper.

notes_for_editor: Agency conflict: FFLOS credits the Oregon Department of Forestry; firelookout.com and Rex's page put the tower at the Forest Service compound, and Wikipedia calls the station a Forest Service facility in the Mount Hood National Forest. Build year: 1933 (Rex's page, firelookout.com) vs 1934 (FFLOS). The FFLOS point (45.45706, -121.12616) and the firelookout.com index point (45.45742, -121.12364) are about 200 m apart. Access level 'restricted' is inferred from the working compound; no source states it. No removal date appears in any source. The brief's ODF agency is left unchanged.
